text:
sasha: FYI seeing 15-25% tail latency regressions on TP fused-attn runs when seq_len > 2048. Only on 8-way TP. Repro script below, small flame attached.

sasha: repro command: `python bench.py --model redwood-3b-fused --tp 8 --batch 4 --seq 4096 --profile=nvtx`

sasha: quick log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-17 14:12:03] step=120 qkv_allgather: 1.8ms -> 12.6ms  (gpu0)
[2026-03-17 14:12:03] flash_attn_fallback: true  (selected kernel: unfused_gemm)
[2026-03-17 14:12:03] NCCL allgather latency: 2.1ms -> 9.7ms
```

joel: ugh. do we have a flame or timeline? can you upload the nvprof/Nsight capture? cc @tanvi

sasha: uploaded: perf-bot:link/flame/1798504321 (nvtx timeline + sysmem counters). main thing: heavy NCCL spikes aligned with the QKV allgather start. compute stalls while waiting for allgather.

perf-bot: automated-note: timeline uploaded, peak GPU utilization drop detected at 14:12:03, kernel switch count increased by 3x compared to baseline. Suggested tags: `tp`, `qkv`, `allgather`, `flash-attn`.

tanvi: quick hypothesis: kernel selection heuristics are picking flash-attn for local shards but the QKV layout after scatter is non-contiguous in memory for some TP placements, causing fallback to unfused GEMM mid-run. fallback + extra allgather overhead explains both the kernel change and the NCCL spikes.

anya: can you paste the per-shard qkv stride? I remember a similar issue where KV cache fragment sizes changed alignment and broke the packer.

sasha: per-shard qkv strides from debug build: `q_stride=[2048, 2048, 2048, 2048, 4096, 4096, 4096, 4096]` — looks like shards 4-7 double stride after a repack path.

joel: that smells like a KV cache fragmentation/repacking artifact. When sequence grows past the pack boundary we trigger the fallback repacker which copies into a differently aligned buffer. If the kernel selector checks only model config but not runtime stride, it will still attempt fused path and then fallback when it sees non-contig tensors. We should make selector peek at tensor metadata prelaunch.

tanvi: agreed. two actionable items: (1) make kernel_selector check .is_contiguous() and stride pattern for q/k/v tensors, and prefer unfused earlier if not contiguous; (2) fix KV repacker to preserve original stride or emit a contiguous view. (3) add a microbenchmark for TP+KV repack cases.

joel: I can take (1). quick patch idea: in choose_kernel_for_attn() add a fast-path: if any(qkv_stride % 256 != 0) or not contiguous -> mark `allow_flash=false`. avoids runtime fallback cost.

sasha: that will reduce wasted launch attempts, but we still have the allgather latency. The timeline shows big NCCL gaps when we hit fallback because the CPU-side repack blocks the progress of the MVAPICH enqueuer on GPU0. Need to decouple repack to async memcpy or schedule repack onto a separate stream.

anya: async repack SGTM. Also we should consider overlapping the allgather with repack: currently we do scatter -> repack -> allgather; maybe we can do scatter -> launch allgather on raw shards, and repack locally after allgather finishes (i.e., post-process). Risky but could hide comm latency.

joel: risky because fused kernels expect packed layout during compute. If we post-repack we must ensure we don't delay compute start. But we could start allgather while launching a lightweight verify kernel that computes checksums to validate order.

perf-bot: automated-suggestion: compare two strategies on a microbench: (A) pre-repack then allgather (current), (B) allgather raw then post-repack, (C) async repack on separate stream + attempt flash with contingency. Perf simulation attached.

sasha: I ran a quick local microbench for (A)/(C) on 8xA100-local: results: (A) median step=8.2ms tail=13.1ms, (C) median=7.9ms tail=10.2ms. So async repack wins on tails. (B) had correctness issues on some ops.

tanvi: ok prioritize (1) selector fix and (2) async repack integration. Also add a metric to runtime tracing: `repack_type` and `kernel_attempts` so we can correlate.

joel: created draft PR branch `tp-qkv-selector` and pushed tests that check contiguousness. link: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/9871 (WIP).

sasha: added perf numbers to the PR comment and upload nvprof traces. PR CI shows a small perf regression on 4-way TP for tiny sequences (seq<128) because the selector now biases away from flash-attn for some borderline strides.

anya: can we add a fallback delta table keyed by (seq_len, tp, stride) so selector is config+data-driven? that way we avoid hard heuristics.

tanvi: yes, we'll collect traces and populate a small CSV that selector consults. low effort to add a model-specific override too.

joel: action items summary:
- joel: implement contiguousness check in selector PR (in progress).
- tanvi: prototype async repack stream and add tracing flags (start today).
- sasha: run long-run microbench for 48h on 8xTP to collect stride table and upload traces.
- anya: write CSV schema and ingestion code for selector overrides.

sasha: thanks. tagging this thread into an incident:perf ticket. perf-bot create ticket: true

perf-bot: ticket created: PERF-2026 - TP QKV scatter/repack causing flash-attn fallback and NCCL tail spikes. assignees: joel, tanvi, anya. priority: P1.

joel: will update PR and post short repro script that toggles `ALLOW_FLASH=true/false` at runtime. thanks all :thumbsup:

sasha: good sync. i'll post follow-up with 48h results.
